title: ConceptLab
excerpt: ConceptLab inspects the concepts and implication rules of small object-attribute tables. Python integer masks and browser JavaScript sets compute independent reports. Three modes separate a complete table, explicit unknown cells and observations checked against a supplied expert table. No model, API or private data is used.

title: Correlab: what does the player know?
excerpt: Correlab audits a supplied joint play distribution in a small two-player general-sum game. It computes exact rational gains for fixed-action, recommendation-conditioned and full-swap deviations. A separate private-signal model lets a player pass or override through a trusted executor. No model is trained, and no equilibrium is searched for.
headings: Correlab: what does the player know?

title: CPNetLab: what follows from the preference rows?
excerpt: CPNetLab takes a small supplied binary CP-net and lists its legal single-variable improving flips. It computes reachability paths, inconsistency cycles, compatible strict rankings and witnesses for incomparable outcomes. A separate whole-row analysis asks which conditional statements support a path or conflict, and which withdrawals restore consistency.
headings: CPNetLab: what follows from the preference rows?
A local improvement is not a score increase

title: CredalLab: one probability model, different questions
excerpt: CredalLab checks finite probability assumptions and compares decisions under those assumptions. Both inspectors use one shared joint distribution. The probability inspector asks whether the supplied bounds can hold together. The decision inspector asks which actions survive several classical rules, and why those rules can disagree.
headings: CredalLab: one probability model, different questions
Why pairwise defenses do not settle a decision
Why individually valid probabilities can conflict

title: CTCLab
excerpt: CTCLab makes two parts of CTC inspectable: summing paths for a target, and losing paths during prefix search. The target atlas computes likelihood, posteriors and logit gradients from synthetic logits. The prefix inspector uses exact rational frame probabilities to track surviving and discarded mass. Neither runs a speech model.
headings: A path is not a transcript

title: CutLab
excerpt: Exact binary energy, flow and all minimum-cut witnesses.

title: DecodeLab
excerpt: Inspectable decoding from scratch: stable staged sampling, complete finite continuation trees and beam-pruning witnesses. Dependency-free Python and independent scalar JavaScript, without a model API.

title: DenoiseLab: learned reconstruction with strong observed-pixel controls
excerpt: DenoiseLab's two-pixel retrieval map now shows exact rational closed minimum cells over two observed values, including area, segment-only, point-only and explicitly proved empty regions. Fraction/BigInt witnesses retain all 3,062 original fitting-row coefficients.
headings: DenoiseLab: learned reconstruction with strong observed-pixel controls

title: DFALab: learn the missing distinction
excerpt: A finite sample can make two protocol states look identical. A closed and consistent observation table can still propose the wrong language. What experiment distinguishes the states, and what evidence justifies stopping?
headings: DFALab: bounded conformance, not an unrestricted test-pass claim
DFALab: exhaustive finite fault atlas and exact test-subset selection

title: Diagnoselab: all conflicts, all minimal repairs
excerpt: Given fixed hard CNF and removable soft clauses, enumerate every relative minimal unsatisfiable subset (MUS) and every minimal correction set (MCS). A repair must hit every core, not merely one. Inclusion-minimal does not mean minimum cardinality or minimum cost. The default control contrasts one removal at cost 5 with two removals costing 2.
headings: Diagnoselab: all conflicts, all minimal repairs
Why one conflict is not enough

title: DiffuseLab: audit a learned reverse process
excerpt: Learned 2-D diffusion from scratch, now with selected-grid DDIM sampling and exact denoiser-call audits. The same 482-parameter model uses 8/16/64 DDIM steps without retraining. Eight steps saves 87.5% of predictor calls but has worse symmetric reference distance here (0.210661 vs DDPM 0.037103), despite a slightly higher near-center fraction.
headings: DiffuseLab: audit a learned reverse process

title: DigitLab: real digits, stronger baseline, bounded attacks
excerpt: Real UCI digit training in NumPy with manual gradients and a frozen official-test audit. On 1,797 test digits, exact 1NN gets 1,760 correct, the tanh MLP 1,734 and linear softmax 1,698, all using the same 3,062 fitting examples.
headings: DigitLab: real digits, stronger baseline, bounded attacks
v0.5: the reference changes the attribution question
v0.4: inspect the trained models, with no prediction server
v0.3: exact radius infima and boundary attainment
The baseline wins on clean digits
Better clean accuracy does not certify input robustness

title: DistillLab: knowledge distillation from scratch, measured against matched control arms
excerpt: A small model trained on a teacher's soft outputs often beats the same model trained on hard labels - the classic explanation is "dark knowledge": the teacher's per-sample class-similarity structure.
headings: DistillLab: knowledge distillation from scratch, measured against matched control arms
Measured results (checked-in fixture, pinned in tests)
v0.3: keep the confidence, change the tail

title: DPPLab: every finite subset, exactly
excerpt: Exact-rational finite DPP subset laws with every determinant, inclusion-kernel witness, Schur include/exclude conditioning and fixed-total-size contrast. Dependency-free Python and independent BigInt JavaScript agree on 24 complete reports / 4,050 exact leaves; 24 Python tests on 3.10-3.13 and actual-Chrome full-record/geometry checks.

title: DriftLens
excerpt: A dependency-free Python CLI/API for standard RBF MMD two-sample tests. The package also has a separate exact supplied-Gram kernel-family mode. 58 Python tests and four Node tests cover both modes; CI uses Python 3.10-3.13. The offline demo asserts passing and failing gate behavior.
headings: A fixed kernel and explicit assumptions

title: EmbedKit: inside the sampled step
excerpt: EmbedKit now audits the noise behind its negatives. The unchanged sampler excludes positive context and earlier negatives, retries20 times, then returns the first eligible sorted word.
headings: Original model, not a selected projection

title: EpistemLab: true when said, false after heard
excerpt: A public announcement can be truthful and make its own content false. EpistemLab shows every world removed, every surviving information block, and the newly evaluated truth set of every subformula. In the default two-world experiment, "p, but agent a does not know p" retains one world and becomes false there. The fact remains true; the ignorance does not.
headings: EpistemLab: true when said, false after heard
EpistemLab disclosures: a restriction is not an announcement
EpistemLab0.3: the fact stays, who saw it changes

title: ErgodLab
excerpt: Exact stationary policy sensitivities, independently checked against directed spanning trees, with a Poisson-bias and temporal reward-variance audit.

title: EUFLab
excerpt: Same output. Not the same input. Proof-producing ground equality, congruence-derived contradictions and total finite countermodels.

title: EvalForge - case study
excerpt: EvalForge runs command adapters against supplied checks and compares saved task results. Its browser inspectors let you edit paired results or a clustered candidate family, then inspect the complete calculation. A passing comparison means the configured regression rule passed, not that a model is good.
